page_title: Realtime Django Part 5: Build a Chat application RabbitMQ and uWSGI websockets (uWSGI WebSockets)

summary.title: Realtime Django Part 5: Build a Chat application RabbitMQ and uWSGI websockets (uWSGI WebSockets)
summary.one_liner: You learn how to push Django chat messages to browsers in real time by routing notifications through RabbitMQ fanout exchanges and serving WebSockets from uWSGI, then scale it with gevent.
keywords: how do i send realtime messages in django
takeaways: Django's WSGI request-response model cannot push messages, so WebSockets need a different server or protocol layer such as ASGI (django-channels) or uWSGI's built-in WebSocket support.
Notifications are published to a RabbitMQ fanout exchange named after the chat session URI, and per-client queues bound to that exchange receive every message (Pub/Sub).

uWSGI's websocket API uses websocket_handshake to upgrade the connection, websocket_recv_nb to receive while sending pong heartbeats, and websocket_send to deliver messages; failed sends kill the process so unacknowledged messages stay queued.

Concurrency is raised by using gevent with monkey.patch_all, where more gevent threads per process and more processes multiply the number of concurrent clients; the author notes this should be profiled first.
Scaling out is done by load balancing several uWSGI WebSocket servers behind Nginx, and RabbitMQ can be clustered separately.
summary.summary: The author explains why Django's request-response WSGI model struggles with WebSockets and compares approaches such as django-channels (ASGI, Daphne, Redis/RabbitMQ channel layers) with a lower-level design that reads RabbitMQ queues directly. The tutorial walks through installing django-notifs and RabbitMQ, writing a custom channel that publishes chat messages to a fanout exchange, and setting up Celery with CELERY_TASK_ALWAYS_EAGER. It then builds a websocket.py consumer that binds queues to the exchange and forwards messages to browsers through uWSGI's WebSocket API, with a Vue Chat component connecting to it. The final sections cover scaling with gevent greenlets and processes, and the post previews the next part on loading screens, auto-scroll, sounds and JSON tokens.
